root_idea.summary: The root centers on bringing something into growth or development, concretely through sowing and the emergence of cultivated produce.
root_idea.development: Its semantic field extends from casting seed and the crop that results to cultivation, growers, offspring, and figurative harvests, while these developments are not automatically meanings of every derived form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized from the imperfect QAC lemma تَزْرَعُ to the Form I perfect citation form زَرَعَ.
Displayed under the standard nominal citation form زَرْعٌ.
Normalized from the Quranic plural active participle to the singular citation form زَارِعٌ.
زُرَّاعٌ is identified in the lexical evidence as the plural of زَارِعٌ and represents the same active-participial lexeme.

senses.definition: To sow or plant by casting seed.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use describes human sowing or planting, including the sowing of a crop; the form may also be transitive with the plant or produce concerned.

senses.definition: To cause seed-produce to grow, vegetate, or germinate.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, human beings are associated with sowing as a means, while the actual causing of growth is attributed to God.

senses.definition: Sown produce or crops; cultivated growth, whether standing or reaped, and often the sown field itself.
senses.usage_conditions: The term predominantly applies to grain such as wheat and barley but can also denote plants or herbage raised by sowing. Quranic contexts include crops, cultivation, and cultivated fields.

senses.definition: A sower or cultivator; figuratively, one who cultivates and advances a cause.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural زُرَّاعٌ in 48:29, the expression refers figuratively to Muhammad and his Companions as inviters to Islam.

senses.definition: One who causes seed-produce to grow, or serves as the human agent or means of its growth.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural in 56:64 occurs in a contrast between human sowing and the ultimate causing of growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To plough up, till, or cultivate land in preparation for sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the land-preparation and cultivation use of the Form I verb, distinct from simply casting seed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To implant or engender something figuratively, especially love in hearts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of sowing, as when generosity and good character are said to sow love in people's hearts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a child or offspring to grow sound and strong, or to grow up for goodness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a supplication or blessing with God as the causer of the child's healthy or virtuous growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To obtain an increase or property after adversity or want.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic passive-like use describing improvement or acquisition after hardship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A contract to till and sow land in return for a specified share of its produce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The seed is supplied by the landowner; the term denotes the mutual agricultural arrangement and its associated bargain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant or seed-produce, to grow from its seed, become tall or leafy, and reach the time for reaping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV verb describes stages of a plant's development or its becoming ready for harvest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of people, to have seed-produce available or to reach a season in which they can make use of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression concerns access to seed-produce or the agricultural season, rather than the act of sowing itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or make haste toward evil or mischief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with إِلَى الشَّرِّ in the cited conventional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask God to bring one's offspring up in piety and to provide lawful sustenance for them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X supplicatory construction seeking divinely fostered moral growth and provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Offspring, children, or a child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use treating descendants as the produce of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's seed or seminal fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended bodily and generative use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fruit or harvest of a person's conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression treats deeds as what one has sown and their consequences as the resulting harvest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which seed may be sown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the availability or absence of a place suitable for sowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apparently, an ear of corn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported, apparently specialized use; it is kept distinct from the ordinary place-for-sowing meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seed or grain intended for sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the seed supplied for planting a field.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The young one of a partridge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seed-produce watered by rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of rain-fed growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything soft or tender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison with tender, rain-grown produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The business or occupation of sowing, tilling, or cultivating land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun denotes agriculture as an activity or occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing sown, especially grain used for sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun refers to the seed or grain as an item intended to be planted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calumniator who sows rancour among friends.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intensive-agent use based on sowing discord in people's hearts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Growth arising in land left unsown for a year or more from grain scattered during harvest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for self-sown or volunteer growth in fallow land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a particular dog; in the expression أَوْلَادُ زَارِعٍ, dogs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a proper-name and resultant collective use, unrelated to the ordinary active-participle meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of cultivation or a place containing sown produce; in one usage, land that is sown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes an agricultural place or plot rather than the crop itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which results are produced for later harvest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression that calls the present world the cultivation-place of the Hereafter, the agricultural image is used figuratively for deeds and their consequences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who raises seed-produce for himself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form VIII active participle carries a self-directed or personally appropriative sense of raising a crop.

cautions: The Form I Quranic verb is displayed under the normalized perfect citation form زَرَعَ, although the supplied occurrences are imperfect second-person plural forms.

The Quranic زُرَّاعٌ group is merged into the active-participle entry زَارِعٌ because the lexical evidence explicitly identifies it as that lexeme's plural. The contextual English renderings are used only as examples, not as independent sense evidence.
